note: Records that would confirm or refute each hypothesized mechanism (Addendum 2 acceptance: 'which records would confirm/refute it'). Investigation prompts, not findings.

confirm_with: Surveyed shoreline/edge elevations below the event water level along a continuous path to the road
High-water marks or photos showing overland flow from the bay side (e.g. USGS 2018 records)
refute_if: Surveyed edge is above the event water level with no opening
Road floods during rain at normal tide with no overland connection

confirm_with: Owner drainage plans tracing corridor inlets to an outfall whose invert is below high-tide levels
Flood dates that coincide with high tide plus rainfall (NOAA gauge 8443970)
refute_if: Outfall invert above relevant tide levels, or a working tide gate confirmed

confirm_with: Field inspection finding debris/sediment in corridor basins
Owner cleaning log entries followed by ponding clearing
refute_if: Basins found clear and taking water while ponding persists (e.g. 311 closure note 'all are taking water')

confirm_with: Hydraulic calculation showing inlet/pipe capacity below design-storm runoff
Repeated ponding with verified clean inlets at normal tide
refute_if: Calculated capacity exceeds runoff for observed storms
Ponding only at high tide (points to tailwater instead)

confirm_with: Survey showing a low point without an inlet where ponding is reported
refute_if: Inlets located at surveyed low points and functioning

confirm_with: Event records showing different drivers on different dates
refute_if: One mechanism confirmed and the others refuted by the checks above
